title: Tomorrow Uses Old Footage
evidence_boundary: Episodic remembering and imagining possible futures recruit overlapping hippocampal and default-network systems, and severe episodic-memory impairment can reduce richly detailed future simulation. This script does not claim memory literally travels through time or that dread is always a memory artifact.
desired_movement: From treating memory as a record of the past to recognizing it as a prediction system that furnishes expectations for the future.
invitation: Which old scene is doing the lighting on the thing you are dreading?
end_card_question: Which old scene is lighting the thing you're dreading?
voice_standard: Liam - warm, curious, a brilliant friend at midnight. Wry through the editor and trailer beats, measured through the memory-loss evidence, spacious and intimate through the turn. Near-whisper on the closing question.

scenes.text: The strangest thing about memory is that it may spend less time preserving yesterday than quietly building the trailer for tomorrow.
scenes.visual: a dim film archive with reels stacked on metal shelves

scenes.text: We treat remembering like opening a drawer. You reach in, you pull out what happened, you put it back.
scenes.visual: a wooden drawer sliding open in a quiet room

scenes.text: But the brain does not store the past like a file. It rebuilds it, every time, out of parts.
scenes.visual: a mosaic being assembled from scattered fragments

scenes.text: And here is the part that changes things. The same machinery that rebuilds yesterday is the machinery that imagines tomorrow.
scenes.visual: two projector beams crossing in a dark hall

scenes.text: Picture memory as a film archive with a restless editor in the back room.
scenes.visual: an editing bench with strips of film hanging on hooks

scenes.text: The editor is not preserving the movies. The editor is cutting trailers.
scenes.visual: scissors trimming a length of celluloid under a lamp

scenes.text: Trailers for films that have not been shot yet.
scenes.visual: an empty cinema screen glowing white in the dark

scenes.text: So an old painful scene does not stay a scene. It becomes lighting. It becomes music. It becomes the expected ending you carry into the next room.
scenes.visual: stage lights shifting color across an empty set

scenes.text: You walk into a conversation that has never happened, already knowing how it goes. That is not intuition. That is footage.
scenes.visual: an open doorway with light spilling into a hallway

scenes.text: People with severe episodic memory loss show something remarkable. They struggle to remember their past in rich detail.
scenes.visual: a photo album with several pages left blank

scenes.text: And they struggle, in the same way, to imagine their future in rich detail.
scenes.visual: a horizon flattening into pale fog

scenes.text: The archive and the trailer come from the same room.
scenes.visual: one lamp lighting two doorways at once

scenes.text: Which means memory is not really about the past. It is a prediction engine that happens to be furnished with old footage.
scenes.visual: gears turning behind a translucent panel

scenes.text: And that reframes something ordinary. When you dread a thing that has not happened, you are not seeing tomorrow.
scenes.visual: rain gathering on a dark window at night

scenes.text: You are watching a cut of yesterday, colour-graded to look like a forecast.
scenes.visual: a colour-grading wheel shifting a scene from warm to cold

scenes.text: This is not a claim that memory travels through time. It does not. Nothing here reaches forward and touches an actual future.
scenes.visual: a still pendulum hanging motionless

scenes.text: It is smaller and stranger than that. The same neural systems light up whether you are recalling or imagining.
scenes.visual: a soft constellation of lights pulsing in sequence

scenes.text: So the question stops being: what do I remember? And becomes: what is my editor putting in the trailer?
scenes.visual: a hand pinning a single frame to a lightbox

scenes.text: Because you can notice the cut. You can catch the moment the old footage gets spliced into a scene that has not started.
scenes.visual: a splice being made between two strips of film

scenes.text: Not to erase it. The archive is yours. It earned its place.
scenes.visual: a labelled reel resting in an open canister

scenes.text: But a trailer is not a prophecy. It is a selection. And selections can be re-cut.
scenes.visual: a stack of frames being reordered on a bench

scenes.text: So come back here for a second. The chair under you. The light in this room. The next hour, which has no footage yet.
scenes.visual: an ordinary chair beside a bright window

scenes.text: What would you find if you asked, honestly, which old scene is doing the lighting on the thing you are dreading?
scenes.visual: dawn light spreading slowly across a plain floor
